metadata.title: Device Identity

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for uniquely identifying devices and binding identity to execution context and lifecycle.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Embedded systems, autonomous devices, cyber‑physical platforms, sensors, actuators, and device identity mechanisms.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Foundational Zero Trust pattern defining device identity as a prerequisite to trust evaluation, not as proof of correctness or safety.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines device identity as attribution and binding data, not as authorization or permission.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Establishes identification capabilities for IoT and device classes.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Guidance for device identity, enrollment, and ownership binding.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Defines integrity‑anchored identity expectations for platforms and devices.

metadata.remarks: Device Identity defines how devices are uniquely identified and bound to an execution and lifecycle context. This pattern does not assert device correctness, safety, authorization, or mission suitability.

components.title: Device Unique Identification
components.description: Assignment of a persistent, non‑ambiguous identity to a device instance.

components.title: Identity‑to‑Device Binding
components.description: Binding of identity to physical or logical device attributes and execution context.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Device identity is bound to platform and integrity anchors.

components.title: Device Identity Lifecycle
components.description: Governance of identity from provisioning through decommissioning.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Device identity is managed throughout its lifecycle.

components.title: Device Identity Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what possession of a device identity does not grant or imply.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Device identity does not imply authorization, correctness, safety, or trustworthiness.
